paper_metadata.title: Crystal structures, mechanical properties, and electronic structure analysis of ternary FeCrAl alloys

evidence.quote: Ternary FeCrAl alloys are key structural materials for high-temperature applications, recognized for their exceptional oxidation resistance and mechanical strength.

Structural search results led to the successful identification of four new ternary FeCrAl alloy structures: a tetragonal FeCrAl phase (space group: I4mm, No. 107), a trigonal FeCrAl phase (space group: P3m1, No. 156), and two orthorhombic FeCrAl phases (space group: Cmcm, No. 63).
The formation energy of the ternary FeCrAl alloys is calculated follows: Ef = {E(FeCrAl) - E(Fe) - E(Cr) - E(Al)}/3

During the structure prediction process using CALYPSO, a population size of 50 was set to ensure thorough search space exploration. The maximum number of evolutionary iterations was set to 30. Moreover, a local PSO algorithm was employed, performing three rounds of local optimization for each structure to refine its energy and geometric configuration.

To ensure accuracy, the plane wave cutoff energy for all ternary FeCrAl alloys was set to 400 eV, achieving good convergence of the total energy, with an energy convergence criterion of 1 × 10-2 eV/atom. During structural optimization, both the lattice parameters and atomic positions of the crystal structure were fully relaxed. Moreover, specific k-point meshes were defined for the different ternary FeCrAl alloy structures: the k-point meshes for the orthorhombic (Cmcm-1 and Cmcm-2) FeCrAl phases were set to 12 × 3 × 8 and 8 × 4 × 8, respectively; the k-point mesh for the trigonal (P3m1) FeCrAl phase was set to 12 × 12 × 4; and the k-point mesh for the tetragonal (I4mm) FeCrAl phase was also set to 12 × 12 × 4.
